project.name: ccbot
project.description: CCBot — a Telegram bot that lets you monitor, interact with, and manage Claude Code sessions running in tmux from Telegram. Each Telegram topic maps 1:1 to a tmux window with a Claude session; it reads terminal output, sends keystrokes, renders screenshots, transcribes voice via OpenAI, and handles interactive UI prompts via inline keyboards.

nodes.name: auth.py
nodes.summary: Thin backward-compatibility re-export of auth/topic helpers (get_thread_id, is_user_allowed) whose canonical definitions live in ccbot.session_guard (ISS-002); adds no logic of its own.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure re-export barrel module; keep implementations in the canonical module.

nodes.name: callback_data.py
nodes.summary: Central definition of all CB_* callback prefixes, typed frozen dataclass payloads, and encode/parse helpers that enforce Telegram's 64-byte callback_data limit for every inline keyboard in the bot.

nodes.name: callback_directory.py
nodes.summary: Routed sub-handlers for the directory browser (db:*): enter subdirectory, navigate up, page, confirm, and cancel, all gated by the stale-topic guard with user_data caching and session picker hand-off.

nodes.name: callback_history.py
nodes.summary: Routed handler for history pagination callbacks (hp:/hn:): parses HistoryCallback data, resolves the tmux window, and edits the current message with the requested history page.

nodes.name: callback_interactive.py
nodes.summary: Table-driven handler for interactive-UI actions (aq:*): maps each CB_ASK_* prefix to a tmux key sequence or a refresh-only display, then re-renders the interactive window via interactive_ui.

nodes.name: callback_pickers.py
nodes.summary: Routed handlers for session/window pickers (rs:*, wb:*): resume existing sessions, start new ones, bind unbound tmux windows to topics, forward pending text, and transition into the directory browser flow.

nodes.name: HistoryCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass payload for history pagination (hp:/hn:) with field validation and on-wire serialization.

nodes.name: DirSelectCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for directory-browser entry selection (db:sel:<index>).

nodes.name: DirPageCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for directory-browser page navigation (db:page:<page>).

nodes.name: WinBindCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for window-picker binding (wb:sel:<index>).

nodes.name: SessionSelectCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for session-picker resumption (rs:sel:<index>).

nodes.name: AskCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for interactive-UI actions (aq:<action>:<window_id>) with prefix validation.

nodes.name: ScreenshotRefreshCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for screenshot refresh (ss:ref:<window_id>).

nodes.name: KeyCallback
nodes.summary: Frozen payload for screenshot control keys (kb:<key_id>:<window_id>).

nodes.name: safe_callback_data
nodes.summary: Serializes callback data (string or typed payload) with an explicit 64-byte UTF-8 limit check that raises instead of truncating.

nodes.name: encode_history_page
nodes.summary: Builds a HistoryCallback wire string for a history page given older/next direction, page, window and byte range.

nodes.name: parse_history
nodes.summary: Parses hp:/hn: callback data into a HistoryCallback, supporting legacy page:window_id forms and current page:window_id:start:end forms.

nodes.name: parse_dir_select
nodes.summary: Parses db:sel:<index> into a DirSelectCallback or None on failure.

nodes.name: parse_dir_page
nodes.summary: Parses db:page:<page> into a DirPageCallback or None on failure.

nodes.name: parse_win_bind
nodes.summary: Parses wb:sel:<index> into a WinBindCallback or None on failure.

nodes.name: parse_session_select
nodes.summary: Parses rs:sel:<index> into a SessionSelectCallback or None on failure.

nodes.name: parse_screenshot_refresh
nodes.summary: Parses ss:ref:<window_id> into a ScreenshotRefreshCallback or None on failure.

nodes.name: parse_ask
nodes.summary: Parses an aq:<action>:<window_id> payload for a known prefix into an AskCallback.

nodes.name: parse_key
nodes.summary: Parses kb:<key_id>:<window_id>, tolerating colons inside window_id.

nodes.name: _handle_dir_select
nodes.summary: Directory browser: enters the selected subdirectory (looked up by index from the cached listing) and re-renders the browser.

nodes.name: _handle_dir_up
nodes.summary: Directory browser: navigates one level up to the parent directory and re-renders.

nodes.name: _handle_dir_page
nodes.summary: Directory browser: switches the visible page of the cached subdirectory listing.

nodes.name: _handle_dir_confirm
nodes.summary: Directory browser: confirms the current path; shows the session picker when sessions exist in the directory, otherwise creates and binds a new window directly.

nodes.name: _handle_dir_cancel
nodes.summary: Directory browser: clears browse and pending-thread state and cancels the flow.

nodes.name: _handle_history
nodes.summary: History pagination callback: parses the HistoryCallback, finds the tmux window, and edits the message with the requested page of history.

nodes.name: _handle_ask
nodes.summary: Table-driven interactive-UI callback: dispatches CB_ASK_* prefixes to tmux key presses (with post-key refresh), refresh-only display, or interactive-message clearing.

nodes.name: _handle_session_select
nodes.summary: Session picker: resumes the selected cached session by creating and binding a window with resume_session_id.

nodes.name: _handle_session_new
nodes.summary: Session picker: starts a brand-new session in the selected directory.

nodes.name: _handle_session_cancel
nodes.summary: Session picker: clears picker and pending-thread state and cancels.

nodes.name: _handle_win_bind
nodes.summary: Window picker: binds an existing unbound tmux window to the topic, forwards any pending text, and reports send failures.

nodes.name: _handle_win_new
nodes.summary: Window picker: transitions to the directory browser to create a new session.

nodes.name: _handle_win_cancel
nodes.summary: Window picker: clears picker and pending-thread state and cancels.

nodes.name: callback_router.py
nodes.summary: Central callback query router: authenticates the user, captures the group chat id for supergroup topic routing, and dispatches every CB_* payload through exact-match and prefix route registries to the callback_* sub-handlers.

nodes.name: callback_screenshot.py
nodes.summary: Handlers for screenshot callbacks (sr:*, kb:*): refresh pane captures in place and send quick control keys to the tmux window, re-rendering the PNG screenshot after each interaction.

nodes.name: callback_topic_guard.py
nodes.summary: Shared stale-topic guard for picker/browser callback flows: verifies a callback comes from the topic that started the pending flow, answers with a stale alert on mismatch, and hosts pending-thread state cleanup plus the RouteHandler signature.

nodes.name: command_handlers.py
nodes.summary: Telegram command and topic lifecycle handlers: /start, /history, /screenshot, /unbind, /esc, /usage, topic-closed and topic-edited sync, unknown-slash forwarding to Claude Code, and unsupported-content rejection.

nodes.name: directory_browser.py
nodes.summary: Builds Telegram UIs for session creation: a picker of unbound tmux windows, a paginated directory browser over the filesystem, and a session-resumption picker, with user_data state keys and relative mtime formatting.

nodes.name: history.py
nodes.summary: Sends or edits paginated message history for a tmux window's session, supporting byte-range unread views, MarkdownV2-aware page splitting, read-offset tracking, and an inline prev/next pagination keyboard.

nodes.name: _match_route
nodes.summary: Resolves callback data to a handler: exact-match table first, then prefix table.

nodes.name: callback_handler
nodes.summary: Entry point for all inline keyboards: requires an authorized user, captures the group chat id for topic routing, then dispatches via the route registries.

nodes.name: _handle_screenshot_refresh
nodes.summary: Screenshot refresh callback: recaptures the pane, re-renders the PNG, and edits the message media in place.

nodes.name: _handle_key
nodes.summary: Screenshot key callback: maps a key_id to a tmux key sequence, sends it, then refreshes the screenshot in place.

nodes.name: _check_same_topic
nodes.summary: Stale-topic guard: verifies the callback comes from the topic that started the pending flow, recovering the marker when configured, and answers with a stale alert on mismatch.

nodes.name: _clear_pending_thread
nodes.summary: Drops the pending topic flow markers (_pending_thread_id/_pending_thread_text) from user_data.

nodes.name: start_command
nodes.summary: /start: authorizes the user, clears browser state, and shows the intro text.

nodes.name: screenshot_command
nodes.summary: /screenshot: captures the pane, renders it to PNG, and sends it with the screenshot control keyboard.

nodes.name: unbind_command
nodes.summary: /unbind: detaches the topic from its tmux window without killing the session and clears topic state.

nodes.name: esc_command
nodes.summary: /esc: sends the Escape control character to the window to interrupt Claude.

nodes.name: usage_command
nodes.summary: /usage: sends /usage to the TUI, captures and parses the output, falling back to a raw trimmed capture.

nodes.name: topic_closed_handler
nodes.summary: Topic-closed lifecycle: kills the bound tmux window and always unbinds/clears topic state, silently when nothing is bound.

nodes.name: topic_edited_handler
nodes.summary: Topic-edited lifecycle: syncs a forum topic rename to the tmux window and internal display name.

nodes.name: forward_command_handler
nodes.summary: Forwards any non-bot slash command to the active Claude Code session, clearing the session association after /clear.

nodes.name: unsupported_content_handler
nodes.summary: Rejects non-text/non-photo/non-voice content with a short explanation.

nodes.name: clear_browse_state
nodes.summary: Clears directory-browsing state keys from user_data.

nodes.name: clear_window_picker_state
nodes.summary: Clears window-picker state keys from user_data.

nodes.name: clear_session_picker_state
nodes.summary: Clears session-picker state keys from user_data.

nodes.name: build_window_picker
nodes.summary: Builds the unbound-window picker UI with two-per-row buttons and New Session / Cancel actions.

nodes.name: build_directory_browser
nodes.summary: Builds the paginated directory browser UI with two-folders-per-row layout, page navigation, and up/select/cancel actions.

nodes.name: _relative_time
nodes.summary: Formats a file's mtime as a human-readable relative time (m/h/d ago).

nodes.name: build_session_picker
nodes.summary: Builds the session-resumption picker UI with per-session summaries, message counts, and relative times.

nodes.name: _build_history_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the history pagination keyboard (Older/page/Newer) with byte-range preservation, or None for a single page.

nodes.name: send_history
nodes.summary: Sends or edits paginated message history for a window's session: unread byte-range views, assistant-only filtering, MarkdownV2-safe page splitting, and read-offset updates.

nodes.name: message_sender.py
nodes.summary: Safe Telegram send/edit helpers with automatic MarkdownV2 to plain-text fallback funneled through MessageFormatter and _run_markdown_fallback, consistent RetryAfter re-raise, photo/media-group sending, and disabled link previews.

nodes.name: screenshot_controls.py
nodes.summary: Builds the inline control keyboard shown under terminal screenshots and maps compact key_ids to tmux key sequences and display labels for KB_* callbacks.

nodes.name: window_bind.py
nodes.summary: Creates a tmux window (optionally resuming an existing session), waits for Claude Code's SessionStart hook with per-mode timeouts, applies session-map overrides when needed, binds the topic thread, and forwards pending text.

nodes.name: screenshot.py
nodes.summary: Renders terminal text (with optional full ANSI 16/256/RGB color parsing) into dark-background PNG images using a three-tier font fallback chain, running the CPU-heavy rendering in a thread pool.

nodes.name: session_guard.py
nodes.summary: Shared auth and topic-to-window resolution guards for bot handlers: require_user, require_bound_window_id, and require_session compose into a SessionContext, with a config-based user allowlist and unified UX strings (ISS-007).

nodes.name: strip_sentinels
nodes.summary: Strips expandable-quote sentinel markers for plain-text fallback.

nodes.name: MessageFormatter
nodes.summary: Single source of MarkdownV2 formatting and plain-text fallback conversion used by every send/edit/reply helper.

nodes.name: _run_markdown_fallback
nodes.summary: Tries the MarkdownV2 send call, then falls back to plain text, always re-raising RetryAfter and logging failures with structured context.

nodes.name: send_with_fallback
nodes.summary: Sends a message with MarkdownV2 and plain-text fallback to a chat (optionally into a forum topic).

nodes.name: edit_with_fallback
nodes.summary: Edits a message with MarkdownV2 and plain-text fallback; returns True only on success.

nodes.name: send_photo
nodes.summary: Sends one or more images as a single photo or a media group, logging (not raising) non-rate-limit Telegram errors.

nodes.name: safe_reply
nodes.summary: Replies to a message with MarkdownV2 and plain-text fallback, re-raising final Telegram errors.

nodes.name: safe_edit
nodes.summary: Edits a target message with MarkdownV2 and plain-text fallback (used by callback handlers).

nodes.name: safe_send
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper around send_with_fallback for direct bot+chat sends.

nodes.name: build_screenshot_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the screenshot control keyboard: navigation arrows, Tab/Space/Enter/Esc, Ctrl-C, and a refresh button.

nodes.name: create_and_bind_window
nodes.summary: Creates a tmux window (optionally resuming a session), waits for the SessionStart hook, forces session-map fixes for resumed sessions, binds the thread, and forwards pending text.

nodes.name: _font_tier
nodes.summary: Assigns a font tier (JetBrains/JB, Noto CJK, Symbola) to a character based on codepoint ranges.

nodes.name: _parse_ansi_line
nodes.summary: Splits a line into styled segments by parsing ANSI SGR escape sequences.

nodes.name: _apply_ansi_codes
nodes.summary: Applies ANSI color codes to a TextStyle, covering basic 16 colors, 256-color palette, and RGB extensions.

nodes.name: _approximate_256_color
nodes.summary: Maps a 256-color palette index to an approximate RGB tuple (cube or grayscale).

nodes.name: _split_line_segments_plain
nodes.summary: Splits a plain line into (text, font_tier) segments, merging consecutive same-tier characters.

nodes.name: text_to_image
nodes.summary: Public entry point: renders text (optionally ANSI-colored) onto a dark PNG image via a font fallback chain, run in a thread pool.

nodes.name: get_thread_id
nodes.summary: Extracts the forum thread id from an update, treating General topic id 1 as no-topic.

nodes.name: require_user
nodes.summary: Authorizes the effective user against the config allowlist, answering or replying with the unauthorized message on failure.

nodes.name: require_bound_window_id
nodes.summary: Auth plus topic-to-window id resolution without requiring a live tmux window.

nodes.name: require_session
nodes.summary: Full guard: auth, named-topic check, window resolution, and live tmux window lookup, returning a SessionContext or None.

nodes.name: binding_store.py
nodes.summary: In-memory storage of thread→window bindings and group chat IDs for Telegram topic routing, with byte-for-byte state.json (de)serialization. Pure in-memory dataclass store; persistence is handled by the SessionManager facade.

nodes.name: BindingStore
nodes.summary: Owns thread_bindings (user→thread→window) and group_chat_ids (user:thread→supergroup chat) routing dicts plus their state.json serialization; mutating methods do not persist, leaving save responsibility to the caller.

nodes.name: bot.py
nodes.summary: Telegram bot application factory and lifecycle: builds the PTB Application, registers all command/callback/message handlers, sets the bot command menu, starts the session monitor and status polling task on init, and tears them down on shutdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses python-telegram-bot Application builder with post_init/post_shutdown hooks and an AIORateLimiter; re-exports handler symbols for stable imports.

nodes.name: post_init
nodes.summary: Async application init hook: registers the bot command menu, re-resolves stale window IDs against live tmux windows, pre-fills the rate limiter bucket, starts the SessionMonitor with a message callback wired to handle_new_message, and launches the status polling task.

nodes.name: post_shutdown
nodes.summary: Async shutdown hook that cancels the status polling task, stops all message queue workers, stops the session monitor, and closes the transcription HTTP client.

nodes.name: create_bot
nodes.summary: Builds and returns the PTB Application instance: registers command handlers, callback query routing, forum topic closed/edited handlers, command/text/photo/voice message handlers, and a catch-all for unsupported content.

nodes.name: config.py
nodes.summary: Application configuration loaded from environment variables with layered .env support; exposes a module-level `config` singleton imported by nearly every module and scrubs sensitive env vars from child processes.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.summary: Loads and validates all runtime settings (Telegram token, allowed users, tmux/Claude paths, monitoring intervals, display toggles, OpenAI transcription) from env vars, resolving the Claude projects path with a priority chain and removing sensitive vars from the environment.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dotenv load_dotenv with override=False so the first-loaded .env wins; Config instance is instantiated at module import time.

nodes.name: notifications.py
nodes.summary: Outbound assistant-message routing: delivers NewMessage events from the SessionMonitor to the correct Telegram topic via thread bindings, handing interactive tool messages to a dedicated UI handler and enqueueing content tasks per user.

nodes.name: handle_new_message
nodes.summary: Routes a NewMessage to all users whose thread-bound window maps to the session: special-cases interactive tool_use messages, clears stale interactive UI, respects the show_tool_calls toggle, and enqueues content messages while advancing per-user read offsets.

nodes.name: hook.py
nodes.summary: Claude Code SessionStart hook subcommand: maintains the window↔session mapping in session_map.json under a file lock and can auto-install itself into ~/.claude/settings.json. Deliberately does not import config.py since hooks run inside tmux panes without bot env vars.

nodes.name: _find_ccbot_path
nodes.summary: Locates the ccbot executable for the hook command, preferring PATH lookup and falling back to the Python interpreter's directory (venv installs).

nodes.name: _is_hook_installed
nodes.summary: Checks whether a 'ccbot hook' command entry already exists in Claude's SessionStart hooks inside a parsed settings dict.

nodes.name: _install_hook
nodes.summary: Installs the ccbot hook command into ~/.claude/settings.json (preserving existing settings), skipping if already installed; returns 0 on success and 1 on error.

nodes.name: hook_main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: handles the --install flag or processes a SessionStart hook event from stdin, resolving the tmux window via TMUX_PANE, validating the payload, and atomically updating session_map.json under a flock while removing old-format keys.

nodes.name: monitor_state.py
nodes.summary: Persistence for the session monitor: tracks per-session JSONL byte offsets and file paths in monitor_state.json so incremental reading resumes after restarts without re-sending old messages.

nodes.name: TrackedSession
nodes.summary: Dataclass record for a monitored session holding session_id, JSONL file path, and last read byte offset, with to_dict/from_dict conversion for JSON persistence.

nodes.name: MonitorState
nodes.summary: Persistent store of tracked sessions keyed by session_id with load/save, add/remove/update operations and a dirty flag so frequent poll cycles only write when changed; saves atomically via utils.

nodes.name: session.py
nodes.summary: Core state hub: the SessionManager singleton orchestrates window↔session mappings, thread bindings, per-user read offsets, session_map.json synchronization, tmux keystroke delivery, and message history, delegating storage to dedicated store/repository classes.
nodes.languageNotes: Dataclass facade that composes BindingStore, WindowStateStore, SessionMapRepository and TranscriptReader via property delegates, keeping backward-compatible access while delegating ownership (ISS-005).

nodes.name: SessionManager
nodes.summary: Facade managing all session state: persists state.json, syncs window states from the hook-written session_map, re-resolves stale window IDs at startup, resolves windows to Claude sessions, binds threads, tracks user read offsets, sends keys to tmux windows, and reads message history.

nodes.name: session_map_repository.py
nodes.summary: File-access repository for session_map.json (written by the SessionStart hook): async reads, atomic writes, and the flock read-modify-write discipline shared with the hook to prevent lost updates.

nodes.name: SessionMapRepository
nodes.summary: Owns file access to session_map.json: exposes the map file path and key prefix dynamically from config, reads/writes atomically, and provides mutate_locked for flock-protected read-modify-write cycles (call via asyncio.to_thread from async code).

nodes.name: session_migration.py
nodes.summary: Pure (no I/O, no tmux) startup migration helpers that convert legacy window_name routing keys to canonical @window_id keys and re-resolve or drop stale IDs across state.json and session_map.json stores, keeping the logic unit-testable.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately pure functions so migrations are unit-testable; SessionManager.resolve_stale_ids orchestrates the live tmux data around them.

nodes.name: is_window_id
nodes.summary: Returns True if a key looks like a tmux window ID ('@0', '@12').

nodes.name: StartupMigrationResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass outcome of apply_startup_state_migration carrying the migrated dicts, a changed flag, and a human-readable list of migration events.

nodes.name: build_old_names_snapshot
nodes.summary: Snapshots the old_id→display_name view before mutation so thread bindings and offsets can still resolve stale IDs against the pre-migration names.

nodes.name: apply_startup_state_migration
nodes.summary: Migrates in-memory state (window_states, thread_bindings, user_window_offsets, window_display_names) to live @window_id keys: migrates legacy name keys, re-resolves stale IDs by display name, or drops them — returns a StartupMigrationResult; caller persists if changed.

nodes.name: migrate_session_map_old_format
nodes.summary: Rewrites old-format session_map keys ('session:window_name') to '@window_id' form in place, resolving names against live windows and discarding superseded or orphaned entries.

nodes.name: cleanup_stale_session_map_entries
nodes.summary: Removes session_map entries whose window @id is no longer among the live tmux windows, returning whether anything was removed.

nodes.name: state_needs_legacy_migration
nodes.summary: Detects whether persisted window_states or thread_bindings still contain pre-@id (window_name) keys requiring migration.

nodes.name: session_monitor.py
nodes.summary: Async polling service that watches Claude Code JSONL transcripts: scans session files for active projects, reads new lines via byte-offset tracking (with truncation/corruption recovery), parses entries, and emits NewMessage objects to a callback with cleanup of replaced sessions.
nodes.languageNotes: Poll-loop pattern with asyncio + aiofiles; mtime cache skips unchanged files and binary-mode reads keep byte offsets stable across platforms.

nodes.name: SessionInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a discoverable Claude session with its session_id and JSONL file path.

nodes.name: NewMessage
nodes.summary: Dataclass payload emitted for each new assistant message: text, completeness flag, content type, tool_use metadata, role, and optional embedded image data from tool results.

nodes.name: SessionMonitor
nodes.summary: Async monitor that polls session_map and transcript files: scans projects with active tmux windows, incrementally reads new JSONL lines per byte offset, carries pending tool_use state across cycles, detects session_map changes, cleans up stale sessions, and invokes a message callback.

nodes.name: transcribe.py
nodes.summary: Voice-to-text transcription of Telegram voice messages via OpenAI's audio API using a lazily-initialized httpx client (no OpenAI SDK dependency).

nodes.name: _get_client
nodes.summary: Returns a lazily-initialized singleton httpx.AsyncClient, recreating it when closed.

nodes.name: transcribe_voice
nodes.summary: Posts OGG voice bytes to the OpenAI audio transcriptions endpoint (gpt-4o-transcribe) and returns the trimmed text, raising on HTTP errors or an empty transcription.

nodes.name: close_client
nodes.summary: Closes and clears the singleton httpx client; called during bot shutdown.

nodes.name: transcript_reader.py
nodes.summary: JSONL transcript reading (ISS-005 4d): constructs Claude session file paths from encoded cwds, extracts session summaries, lists sessions per directory, and reads byte-ranged message history with TranscriptParser.

nodes.name: ClaudeSession
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a Claude Code session: session_id, summary text, message count, and JSONL file path.

nodes.name: TranscriptReader
nodes.summary: Reads Claude session transcripts under the projects path: encodes cwds to directory names, resolves session files directly or by glob fallback, scans JSONL for summaries, lists up to 10 recent sessions per directory, and reads byte-ranged message lists.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Shared utilities used across CCBot modules: config directory resolution, crash-safe atomic JSON writes via temp+rename, first-entry cwd extraction from JSONL, and flock helpers with a Windows no-op fallback.
nodes.languageNotes: Provides POSIX fcntl flock with a no-op stub on Windows so unit tests can import on any platform.

nodes.name: ccbot_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves the CCBot config directory from the CCBOT_DIR env var, falling back to ~/.ccbot.

nodes.name: atomic_write_json
nodes.summary: Writes JSON data atomically by writing to a same-directory temp file, fsyncing, then renaming over the target; cleans up the temp file on failure to prevent corruption.

nodes.name: read_cwd_from_jsonl
nodes.summary: Reads the cwd field from the first parseable JSONL entry in a session file; shared by session.py and session_monitor.py.

nodes.name: window_state_store.py
nodes.summary: In-memory storage of window states (window_id → session_id/cwd/name) and display names with byte-for-byte state.json (de)serialization; pure dataclass store whose persistence is the SessionManager facade's job.

nodes.name: WindowState
nodes.summary: Dataclass record of persistent per-window state (session_id, cwd, window_name) with to_dict/from_dict serialization helpers.

nodes.name: WindowStateStore
nodes.summary: Owns window_states and window_display_names dicts with state.json serialization plus get/set/clear window session and display name operations; mutations do not persist by design.

nodes.name: analyze_graph.py
nodes.summary: Analyzes the project knowledge-graph.json to produce hotspot, untested-file, and complex-file signals with per-path scores used to boost backlog prioritization, then writes a JSON report plus Markdown summary to .agentic/out.

nodes.name: analyze_graph
nodes.summary: Core analysis pass: computes fan-in/fan-out and edge-type counts over graph nodes and edges, scores code-file hotspots from complexity, tested, and degree signals, and returns stats, layers, hotspots, orphans, and path scores.

nodes.name: _recommendations
nodes.summary: Generates human-readable refactoring recommendations from hotspot, untested-file, and complex-file signals with project-specific guidance for bot.py hotspots.

nodes.name: render_markdown
nodes.summary: Renders the analysis report as a Markdown document with layers, a top-hotspots table, recommendations, and untested-file samples.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Loads knowledge-graph.json and config via paths helpers, runs analyze_graph, attaches meta, and writes the analysis report JSON and Markdown to the configured output dir.

nodes.name: build_context_pack.py
nodes.summary: Builds a task-scoped subgraph slice (context pack) from knowledge-graph.json by hop-expanding from task seed nodes through the graph adjacency, bounded by node/edge caps, and writes context-pack.json.

nodes.name: _seed_ids
nodes.summary: Determines seed node ids from a task's related_nodes and files lists, matching exact file nodes or directory-prefix node types like file/config/module.

nodes.name: build_context_pack
nodes.summary: Performs breadth-first hop expansion from seed nodes over the undirected adjacency of the graph (capped by max_nodes/max_edges), then slices nodes, edges, and layers into the task context pack with seed ids and task metadata.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Loads graph and backlog, resolves the target task id (selected task by default), builds the context pack, and writes it to context-pack.json in the output dir.

nodes.name: cli.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the agentic pipeline wiring analyze, plan, select, context, status, list, validate, sync-issues, and run commands, plus the propose and human-in-the-loop proposal subcommands registered by propose.py.

nodes.name: cmd_select
nodes.summary: Runs the plan step via prioritize.run then renders the implement prompt, printing the selected task id and artifact paths or failing when no task is selectable.

nodes.name: cmd_validate
nodes.summary: Runs guardrail, quality, and task-evidence validation via validate_changes.run (loading task evidence when a task id is given), printing the JSON verdict and per-check output.

nodes.name: cmd_run
nodes.summary: Runs the full local pipeline analyze, plan, render prompts, build context pack, then workspace validation, with no LLM implement step.

nodes.name: build_parser
nodes.summary: Builds the argparse subcommand parser with metavar help listing every command, and registers propose and human-in-the-loop subcommands from propose.py.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that resolves the repo root, builds the parser, dispatches to command handlers including the propose and HITL handler maps, and returns the exit code.

nodes.name: mcp_server.py
nodes.summary: Stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server (ccbot-agentic) exposing the agentic pipeline as MCP tools for task listing, selection, analysis, context packs, prompts, status updates, validation, and pipeline health checks.

nodes.name: tool_get_context_pack
nodes.summary: MCP tool handler returning a task-scoped context pack via service.get_context_pack with configurable hops and refresh flags.

nodes.name: tool_mark_task_status
nodes.summary: MCP tool handler validating task_id/status arguments and delegating status updates to service.mark_task_status.

nodes.name: tool_run_analyze
nodes.summary: MCP tool handler that lazily imports analyze_graph.run to recompute hotspot analysis and returns a slim summary of stats, hotspots, and recommendations.

nodes.name: _handle_tools_call
nodes.summary: Resolves the requested tool name in the TOOLS registry and invokes its handler, converting any exception into an MCP error payload with a traceback tail.

nodes.name: _dispatch
nodes.summary: Routes JSON-RPC 2.0 methods (initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/prompts list) to protocol-correct responses, ignoring notifications and answering unknown methods with an error.

nodes.name: _read_message
nodes.summary: Reads one framed JSON-RPC message from stdin using Content-Length framing with a newline-delimited JSON fallback.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: MCP server loop: resolves the repo root, reads messages until EOF, dispatches them, and writes Content-Length framed responses to stdout while logging diagnostics to stderr.

nodes.name: paths.py
nodes.summary: Shared path and config resolution helpers: walks parents to locate the repo root (pyproject.toml plus .agentic), loads and writes JSON/text under .agentic, and resolves the configured output dir. This is the common I/O API used by every other agentic script.
nodes.languageNotes: BOM-tolerant JSON reading (utf-8-sig) and ensure_ascii=False writing for non-ASCII content.

nodes.name: find_repo_root
nodes.summary: Walks the starting directory and its parents until it finds a directory containing both pyproject.toml and .agentic/, falling back to scripts/agentic/../.. when none is found.

nodes.name: load_json
nodes.summary: Reads and parses a JSON file, tolerating a UTF-8 BOM.

nodes.name: write_json
nodes.summary: Creates parent directories and writes pretty-printed JSON (indent 2, ensure_ascii False) with a trailing newline.

nodes.name: write_text
nodes.summary: Creates parent directories and writes a UTF-8 text file.

nodes.name: load_config
nodes.summary: Loads the .agentic/config.json pipeline configuration for a repo root, defaulting to the auto-detected root.

nodes.name: out_dir
nodes.summary: Returns the pipeline output directory from the config outputs.dir setting joined onto the repo root.

nodes.name: prioritize.py
nodes.summary: Ranks backlog tasks by combining configured priority weights, dependency satisfaction, and knowledge-graph path-score bonuses, then selects the next task and writes plan.json plus a Markdown plan to .agentic/out.

nodes.name: score_task
nodes.summary: Computes a task score from priority weights plus knowledge-graph path-score bonuses (exact or prefix match) and related-node boosts, marking dependency satisfaction and selectability.

nodes.name: build_plan
nodes.summary: Ranks all backlog tasks, selects the next selectable task (or a forced task id), and returns a plan with ranked_tasks, the selected task, and selection reasons.

nodes.name: render_plan_md
nodes.summary: Renders the plan as a Markdown document showing the selected task, ranked tasks with scores and selectability, and dependency blockers.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Loads config, analysis report, and backlog, runs build_plan, writes plan.json and plan.md to the output dir, and returns the plan.

nodes.name: render_prompt.py
nodes.summary: Renders the implement prompt and PR body from templates using the selected task, writes them to .agentic/out, and bundles policies, the task, and the prompt into an agent-context file.

nodes.name: render_pr_body
nodes.summary: Fills a PR body template with the task's id, problem/solution, acceptance checklist, risk, and graph commit.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Orchestrates prompt rendering: loads the selected task and plan, reads implement/PR templates and policies, and writes implement-prompt.md, pr-body.md, and agent-context.md.

nodes.name: propose.py
nodes.summary: Proposal subsystem implementing propose, import-proposal, show-proposal, reject, approve, request-changes, and apply: captures and validates diffs, enforces guardrails and base-SHA freshness, and manages proposal artifacts under .agentic/out/proposals behind a human-in-the-loop approval gate.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Wraps subprocess.run with command echoing and optional check failure, used for every git and tool invocation in the subsystem.

nodes.name: iter_tasks
nodes.summary: Iterates over backlog tasks yielding (task_id, task) pairs while reconciling proposal status metadata against the tasks.json file.

nodes.name: load_task
nodes.summary: Loads a single task by id from .agentic/backlog/tasks.json, raising a targeted error when the task or file is missing.

nodes.name: update_task_status
nodes.summary: Updates a task's status and status metadata (timestamp, optional proposal id) in the backlog JSON file.

nodes.name: ensure_clean_tree
nodes.summary: Checks that the git working tree is clean (or explicitly allowed dirty) before the proposal flow so diffs are captured from a known state.

nodes.name: render_default_prompt
nodes.summary: Builds the default implementation prompt template for a task, filling in problem, solution, files, acceptance criteria, dependency, and risk placeholders.

nodes.name: latest_proposal_dir
nodes.summary: Finds the newest proposal directory for a task by scanning timestamped proposal directories and their meta.json files, raising when none exists.

nodes.name: resolve_proposal_dir
nodes.summary: Resolves a proposal's target directory from an explicit id or 'latest' keyword, with task-scoped search and targeted errors for missing or mismatched proposals.

nodes.name: capture_working_tree_diff
nodes.summary: Captures the working-tree diff against a base ref via piped git diff output.

nodes.name: list_changed_paths_from_diff
nodes.summary: Parses a unified diff to list changed file paths with their change statuses (added/modified/deleted).

nodes.name: _glob_to_regex
nodes.summary: Converts a guardrail glob pattern into an anchored regular expression for path matching.

nodes.name: _match_glob
nodes.summary: Matches a path against a single glob pattern supporting ** recursion, trailing-slash directory matches, extension wildcards, and negation rules.

nodes.name: path_allowed
nodes.summary: Determines whether a changed path passes the config guardrails, where block patterns win over allow patterns.

nodes.name: _write_temp_diff
nodes.summary: Writes diff bytes to a temporary file so git apply checks can run against it.

nodes.name: check_diff_applies
nodes.summary: Validates that a diff applies cleanly via git apply --check, and rejects when it does not.

nodes.name: diff_numstat
nodes.summary: Runs git diff --numstat on a recorded diff and returns per-file add/delete statistics with metadata, matching it against changed paths.

nodes.name: validate_proposal_diff
nodes.summary: Top-level diff validation: rejects empty diffs, markdown fences, diff comments, and non-unified-diff output, and confirms the diff applies cleanly.

nodes.name: build_files_json
nodes.summary: Builds the proposal files.json from numstat output, enforcing config max files/LOC deltas and the guardrail allow/block lists.

nodes.name: build_risk_json
nodes.summary: Builds a risk-assessment entry for the task from its category, estimated risk, and touched paths.

nodes.name: build_evidence_plan
nodes.summary: Builds an evidence plan mapping files, source patterns, directories, and JSON blobs the task must verify after application.

nodes.name: build_proposal_md
nodes.summary: Renders the human-readable proposal.md from the task, proposal id, base sha, and changed paths.

nodes.name: create_proposal_artifacts
nodes.summary: Creates the full proposal artifact set (diff, files.json, risk, evidence plan, proposal.md, meta) in timestamped directories under .agentic/out/proposals.

nodes.name: prepare_pipeline_context
nodes.summary: Prepares the agentic pipeline context (plan, implement prompt, context pack) needed for task proposals.

nodes.name: _assert_base_sha_fresh
nodes.summary: Verifies the recorded base SHA still matches the current base ref, blocking stale proposals with a clear error.

nodes.name: _assert_feature_branch
nodes.summary: Blocks approve/apply on protected branches (main/master) unless explicitly allowed.

nodes.name: reject
nodes.summary: Writes a reject artifact with the reason and reviewer, leaving the working tree untouched.

nodes.name: approve
nodes.summary: Records approval.json after base-SHA freshness and feature-branch checks, capturing the approver identity and message.

nodes.name: request_changes
nodes.summary: Archives the proposal and saves reviewer notes as a request-changes artifact.

nodes.name: apply
nodes.summary: Applies an approved proposal diff to the working tree only when the base SHA matches, approval exists, and the branch is allowed.

nodes.name: cmd_propose
nodes.summary: Propose command handler: captures the working-tree diff for the task, validates it, and creates the proposal artifacts.

nodes.name: cmd_show_proposal
nodes.summary: Shows proposal artifacts (markdown, files, risk, meta) for the latest or a given proposal.

nodes.name: cmd_import_proposal
nodes.summary: Imports an externally created proposal.diff: validates it, creates artifacts, and finalizes the proposal record.

nodes.name: cmd_reject
nodes.summary: CLI handler for the reject command with --proposal and --reason options.

nodes.name: cmd_approve
nodes.summary: CLI handler for the approve command with --proposal, --message, and approver identity.

nodes.name: cmd_request_changes
nodes.summary: CLI handler for the request-changes command saving reviewer notes.

nodes.name: cmd_apply
nodes.summary: CLI handler for the apply command with --base-ref and --allow-on-main flags.

nodes.name: register_propose_commands
nodes.summary: Registers the propose pipeline subcommands (propose, show-proposal, import-proposal) on the argparse subparser and returns their handler map.

nodes.name: register_hitl_commands
nodes.summary: Registers the human-in-the-loop subcommands (reject, approve, request-changes, apply) with approval-gate semantics and returns their handler map.

nodes.name: service.py
nodes.summary: Shared service layer (single source of truth) used by both the CLI and MCP server: task listing/selection, analysis, context packs, prompts, status updates, validation, and pipeline health checks.

nodes.name: list_tasks
nodes.summary: Lists backlog tasks with an optional status filter, attaches plan ranking scores (soft-falling back to an on-demand plan), and sorts by score descending.

nodes.name: get_task
nodes.summary: Returns a single backlog task by id, raising KeyError when unknown.

nodes.name: select_next_task
nodes.summary: Analyzes the knowledge graph (unless skipped), plans to select the next task, renders prompts and a context pack, and returns the artifacts.

nodes.name: get_analysis
nodes.summary: Returns a slimmed analysis report, recomputing via analyze_graph.run when refresh is requested or the report file is missing.

nodes.name: get_context_pack
nodes.summary: Returns the context pack for a task, rebuilding when refresh is set or the cached pack belongs to another task.

nodes.name: get_implement_prompt
nodes.summary: Returns the rendered implement prompt and PR body from .agentic/out together with the selected task id.

nodes.name: mark_task_status
nodes.summary: Updates a task's status, status timestamp, and optional note in the backlog, validating status values and persisting via paths.write_json.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Runs change validation via validate_changes.run and returns a compact verdict with guardrail, quality, and evidence information.

nodes.name: pipeline_status
nodes.summary: Health check of the pipeline: reports repo root, knowledge graph/backlog presence, generated artifacts, proposals, and the selected task.

nodes.name: sync_issues.py
nodes.summary: Creates or updates GitHub issues from backlog tasks via the gh CLI, mapping tasks to open issues through an agentic-task-id marker comment and supporting dry-run.

nodes.name: _gh
nodes.summary: Runs the gh CLI with args in the repo cwd, capturing output as UTF-8 text without raising on non-zero exit.

nodes.name: _issue_body
nodes.summary: Renders a GitHub issue body from a backlog task including acceptance criteria, file list, metadata JSON, and the agentic-task-id marker.

nodes.name: list_existing_task_issues
nodes.summary: Queries open agentic-labeled issues via gh and maps task ids to issue numbers by parsing the marker line in each body.

nodes.name: sync
nodes.summary: Creates or updates GitHub issues for backlog tasks in the given statuses, dry-run by default, returning the planned actions or gh command output.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Argparse entry point for the sync-issues command with --apply and --statuses flags, printing the sync result as JSON.

nodes.name: update_backlog_status.py
nodes.summary: Local helper CLI to update task status in .agentic/backlog/tasks.json, enforcing done-blocking evidence checks for structural tasks and tasks with evidence blocks.

nodes.name: done_block_reasons
nodes.summary: Computes reasons why a task cannot be marked done: structural tasks need an evidence block and must pass check_evidence against the working tree.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Argparse CLI updating a task's status, blocking done without valid evidence, and persisting timestamps and optional notes.

nodes.name: validate_changes.py
nodes.summary: Validates agent changes: checks path guardrails (allow/ignore/block globs) against git-changed files, runs quality gates (ruff/pyright/pytest) in the venv, and verifies task evidence patterns against the working tree.

nodes.name: _run
nodes.summary: Runs a subprocess with text capture, returning cmd, returncode, ok, and stdout/stderr tails, and handles missing executables.

nodes.name: _ensure_dev_env
nodes.summary: Syncs dev extras via uv when the venv or python is missing so pyright can resolve imports.

nodes.name: _git_changed_files
nodes.summary: Lists files changed against a base ref using git diff (or merge-base diff), with porcelain and status parsing into normalized paths.

nodes.name: _match_any
nodes.summary: Matches a path against a list of glob patterns supporting **/ prefixes, directory suffixes, and fnmatch semantics.

nodes.name: check_guardrails
nodes.summary: Evaluates allow, ignore, and block guardrail lists against changed paths, flagging violations and blocking config breaches or size-limit violations.

nodes.name: check_evidence
nodes.summary: Verifies task evidence against the working tree: file existence, source and path patterns, directory scanning, JSON blob sizes, and regex matches.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs the full validation: changed files via git, guardrails, optional quality gates (ruff/pyright/pytest), then evidence checks, and writes the report to the output dir.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Argparse entry point for the validate command with --base-ref, --skip-quality, and --evidence flags.

nodes.name: json_dumps_summary
nodes.summary: Summarizes the validation report as a single-line JSON verdict with guardrail, quality, and evidence counts.

nodes.name: errors.py
nodes.summary: Centralizes Telegram error classification (expected/stale/transient), logging helpers, and RetryAfter flood-control normalization used across Telegram/tmux hot paths.
nodes.languageNotes: PTB v22+ RetryAfter.retry_after may be a timedelta; retry_after_seconds normalizes both shapes.

nodes.name: log_exception
nodes.summary: Logs an exception with its type name, message, and optional key=value context pairs at a configurable log level.

nodes.name: reraise_retry_after
nodes.summary: Re-raises RetryAfter exceptions unchanged so higher layers can apply flood-control backoff; no-op for all other exceptions.

nodes.name: retry_after_seconds
nodes.summary: Converts a RetryAfter exception to the flood-control wait in seconds, supporting both legacy int and timedelta retry_after values.

nodes.name: capture_registry.py
nodes.summary: Process-wide registry mapping (user_id, thread_id) to active asyncio bash-capture tasks, providing cancel and identity-checked discard so topic teardown never leaves a running watcher behind.

nodes.name: CaptureTaskRegistry
nodes.summary: Stores, cancels, and discards bash-capture asyncio tasks keyed by (user_id, thread_id); discard uses identity checks so a stale watcher cannot evict a newer registration.

nodes.name: cleanup.py
nodes.summary: Unified topic cleanup API that cancels bash capture tasks, clears status/tool-message tracking and interactive UI state, and pops pending user_data when a topic is deleted or its binding goes stale.

nodes.name: clear_topic_state
nodes.summary: Teardown of all per-topic memory state: cancels running capture watchers, clears status/tool message IDs, deletes the interactive UI message, and removes pending thread-state from user_data.

nodes.name: interactive_ui.py
nodes.summary: Detects Claude Code interactive terminal UIs (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, Permission Prompt, RestoreCheckpoint) from captured pane text and renders them in Telegram with navigation keyboards, tracking interactive mode per (user, thread).

nodes.name: set_interactive_mode
nodes.summary: Records the window currently in interactive mode for a user/thread so later messages can refresh that UI.

nodes.name: _build_interactive_keyboard
nodes.summary: Builds the inline navigation keyboard (space/arrows/tab, esc/refresh/enter) for an interactive UI, omitting horizontal keys when the UI name is RestoreCheckpoint.

nodes.name: handle_interactive_ui
nodes.summary: Captures the tmux pane, checks for a Claude Code interactive UI, extracts its content, and sends it as a Telegram message with a navigation keyboard, editing in place when a message already exists.

nodes.name: clear_interactive_msg
nodes.summary: Removes the tracked interactive message for a user/thread, deletes it from the chat when possible, and exits interactive mode.

nodes.name: message_handlers.py
nodes.summary: Telegram message handlers for text, photos, and voice: routes input to bound tmux windows, downloads and forwards images, transcribes voice via OpenAI, and runs background bash-output capture for `!` commands.

nodes.name: photo_handler
nodes.summary: Downloads the highest-resolution photo to the images directory and forwards its path, with optional caption, to the bound Claude Code window.

nodes.name: voice_handler
nodes.summary: Downloads an OGG voice message, transcribes it via the OpenAI-backed transcriber, and forwards the transcript to the bound window with user confirmation.

nodes.name: capture_bash_output
nodes.summary: Background asyncio task that polls the tmux pane for `!` command output, sends the first capture as a new message and edits it in place as output appears, until 30 seconds elapse or the task is cancelled.

nodes.name: text_handler
nodes.summary: Routes user text to the bound tmux window: guards picker/browser/session states, shows window picker and directory browser for unbound topics, injects text into the session, starts `!` bash capture, and refreshes pending interactive UIs.

nodes.name: message_queue.py
nodes.summary: Per-user asyncio message queue system for ordered Telegram delivery: FIFO workers with flood control, content-message merging, status/tool-message tracking, and topic-aware sending via MessageTask.thread_id.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines asyncio.Queue workers, per-user locks, monotonic flood-control timestamps, and in-queue task coalescing for Telegram 4096-char limits.

nodes.name: MessageTask
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a queued message task with type (content/status_update/status_clear), optional thread_id, content parts, tool_use_id, and attached image data.

nodes.name: StatusTracker
nodes.summary: Per-user maps for status message IDs (message_id, window_id, text) and tool_use message IDs, with set/get/pop accessors, clear-for-topic helpers, and full reset.

nodes.name: MessageQueueManager
nodes.summary: Owns per-user asyncio queues, worker tasks, locks, and monotonic flood-control timestamps plus the StatusTracker; provides queue lifecycle, flood queries, and shutdown.

nodes.name: get_message_queue
nodes.summary: Returns the asyncio queue for a user if one exists; part of the stable public wrapper surface over the queue_manager singleton.

nodes.name: get_or_create_queue
nodes.summary: Returns the user's queue, lazily creating it and starting its worker task if it does not yet exist.

nodes.name: clear_status_msg_info
nodes.summary: Clears status-message tracking for a user and optional thread via the shared StatusTracker; used by message handlers and cleanup.

nodes.name: clear_tool_msg_ids_for_topic
nodes.summary: Removes all tool_use to message-ID tracking entries for a topic; used during topic cleanup.

nodes.name: shutdown_workers
nodes.summary: Cancels all queue workers and clears queue state; invoked during bot shutdown.

nodes.name: _inspect_queue
nodes.summary: Non-destructively drains a queue with get_nowait to list its contents so the caller can merge or refill them.

nodes.name: _can_merge_tasks
nodes.summary: Determines whether two consecutive content tasks can be merged, breaking the chain at tool_use/tool_result boundaries and window switches.

nodes.name: _merge_content_tasks
nodes.summary: Merges queued content tasks from the same window into a single task while preserving order and respecting size limits and non-mergeable boundaries.

nodes.name: _process_content_with_retry
nodes.summary: Processes a content task with retry and backoff when Telegram raises RetryAfter flood limits, marking the user's queue as flooded while waiting.

nodes.name: _message_queue_worker
nodes.summary: Per-user worker loop that fetches tasks, merges content tasks, processes them under a lock, honors flood-control waits, and logs exceptions without crashing.

nodes.name: _send_task_images
nodes.summary: Sends image data attached to a content task as Telegram photos to the resolved chat.

nodes.name: _process_content_task
nodes.summary: Delivers a content message: edits earlier tool_use messages via tracked IDs, sends fallback content, sends attached images, and schedules status checks.

nodes.name: _convert_status_to_content
nodes.summary: Promotes a pending status message into a full content message by deleting the status message and sending or editing the real content text.

nodes.name: _process_status_update_task
nodes.summary: Handles status_update tasks: clears stale status messages, sends fresh ones with chat actions, and keeps the StatusTracker maps consistent.

nodes.name: _do_send_status_message
nodes.summary: Sends or edits a status message in the topic with Markdown fallback, updating the StatusTracker and handling delete/send races gracefully.

nodes.name: _do_clear_status_message
nodes.summary: Deletes the tracked status message for a topic and removes its entry from the StatusTracker.

nodes.name: _check_and_send_status
nodes.summary: When a user's queue is idle, polls the tmux pane for a status line and enqueues a status update for the window.

nodes.name: enqueue_content_message
nodes.summary: Builds a content MessageTask (text/parts, optional thread_id and image data) and enqueues it on the user's queue in receive order.

nodes.name: enqueue_status_update
nodes.summary: Enqueues a status_update task, skipping redundant updates while flooded or when the same status is already pending, and enqueuing delete tasks for None text.

nodes.name: status_polling.py
nodes.summary: Background 1s polling loop checking each thread-bound tmux window for Claude Code status lines and interactive UIs, enqueuing updates, and probing topic existence every 60s to kill windows and unbind deleted topics.

nodes.name: update_status_message
nodes.summary: Polls a window's pane: reports missing windows, detects and clears interactive UI states per user/thread, and enqueues status updates unless skip_status is set.

nodes.name: status_poll_loop
nodes.summary: Infinite polling task iterating thread bindings: periodic topic-existence probe (kills windows and unbinds on Topic_id_invalid), stale-binding cleanup, and per-window status updates that skip status when the queue is busy.

nodes.name: terminal_parser.py
nodes.summary: Regex-based parser for captured tmux pane text: detects Claude Code interactive UIs via top/bottom marker patterns, extracts status lines with spinner detection, strips pane chrome, and locates bash command output.
nodes.languageNotes: UI patterns are tuples of compiled regexes to tolerate Claude Code wording changes across versions; first matching pattern wins.

nodes.name: InteractiveUIContent
nodes.summary: Dataclass holding the extracted interactive UI display content and the name of the pattern that matched.

nodes.name: UIPattern
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass pairing top/bottom regex-marker tuples that delimit an interactive UI region, with a minimum line gap; any single marker match suffices.

nodes.name: _try_extract
nodes.summary: Scans lines for a single UI pattern's top and bottom markers and extracts the bounded content region, shortening long separator lines.

nodes.name: extract_interactive_content
nodes.summary: Tries every registered UI pattern in order and returns the first InteractiveUIContent match extracted from the pane text.

nodes.name: is_interactive_ui
nodes.summary: Returns True when extract_interactive_content finds a match; this cheap gate is used by polling and message handlers before rendering a UI.

nodes.name: parse_status_line
nodes.summary: Scans pane text from the bottom up for a spinner-plus-status line and returns the cleaned status text, or None when no status line is present.

nodes.name: strip_pane_chrome
nodes.summary: Removes empty and border-artifact lines around pane content so downstream extraction operates on clean text.

nodes.name: extract_bash_output
nodes.summary: Finds the output following a `!` command sent to a pane, stripping the echoed command line and trailing artifacts.

nodes.name: UsageInfo
nodes.summary: Dataclass carrying the raw /usage panel text and the cleaned parsed lines.

nodes.name: parse_usage_output
nodes.summary: Parses a /usage terminal panel into raw text plus cleaned lines, stripping block-graphic padding characters from each line.

nodes.name: tmux_manager.py
nodes.summary: Async-friendly wrapper around libtmux for a single tmux session: lists and finds windows, captures panes, sends keys, renames, kills, and creates windows while scrubbing sensitive env vars from the session.
nodes.languageNotes: All blocking libtmux calls are wrapped in asyncio.to_thread; session env is scrubbed so child processes like Claude Code never inherit secrets.

nodes.name: TmuxWindow
nodes.summary: Dataclass describing a tmux window: window id, name, cwd, and the command running in its active pane.

nodes.name: TmuxManager
nodes.summary: Singleton managing the tmux session: session get/create with env scrubbing, window discovery and lookup, async pane capture (plain or ANSI via subprocess), key injection, and rename/kill/create lifecycle operations.

nodes.name: response_builder.py
nodes.summary: Builds paginated Telegram response messages from Claude Code output, handling content types (text, thinking, tool_use, tool_result), truncating thinking blocks, and splitting long text into chunks within Telegram's 4096-char limit without doing MarkdownV2 conversion (deferred to the send layer).
nodes.languageNotes: Prefers chunk sizes conservative of the 3000-char budget so MarkdownV2 expansion at the send layer never overflows the message limit.

nodes.name: build_response_parts
nodes.summary: Transforms raw Claude Code output into a list of Telegram-ready markdown strings: prefixes user messages, truncates completed thinking blocks to 500 chars, keeps expandable quote sentinels atomic, converts tables to card-style, and pages long text with [i/N] suffixes.

nodes.name: markdown_v2.py
nodes.summary: Markdown to Telegram MarkdownV2 conversion layer that wraps telegramify_markdown, converts markdown tables into card-style key-value output (skipping tables inside code blocks), and renders expandable blockquotes delimited by TranscriptParser sentinel tokens so the library does not mangle them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a TelegramMarkdownRenderer context manager directly instead of telegramify_markdown.markdownify so module-level token rules are not reset on exit.

nodes.name: convert_markdown_tables
nodes.summary: Rewrites pipe-delimited markdown tables into card-style **Header**: value rows separated by horizontal lines, tracking and skipping fenced code blocks so their contents are untouched.

nodes.name: _render_expandable_quote
nodes.summary: Renders an expandable blockquote match as raw >…|| MarkdownV2 syntax, escaping special characters and truncating line-by-line to stay within the 3800-char rendering budget.

nodes.name: _markdownify
nodes.summary: Custom markdownify pipeline that drives TelegramMarkdownRenderer directly, disabling indented code blocks (only fenced blocks count) while rendering text through mistletoe with latex escaping.

nodes.name: convert_markdown
nodes.summary: Public entry point converting standard Markdown to Telegram MarkdownV2: converts tables to cards, extracts expandable quote segments for dedicated rendering, and markdownifies the remaining text.

nodes.name: telegram_sender.py
nodes.summary: Message splitting utility that chunks long text into Telegram-safe pieces measured in UTF-16 code units (Telegram's length accounting), preferring line boundaries and auto-closing/re-opening fenced code blocks so every chunk stays valid markdown.
nodes.languageNotes: Lengths use UTF-16 code units (emoji and non-BMP chars count as 2), matching Telegram's 4096 limit exactly instead of Python len() code points.

nodes.name: _force_split
nodes.summary: Splits a single overlong line into pieces that each fit within a UTF-16 budget, used as a last resort when a line alone exceeds Telegram's message limit.

nodes.name: split_message
nodes.summary: Splits a message into Telegram-safe chunks up to max_length UTF-16 units, accumulating whole lines where possible, reserving headroom inside code blocks for a closing fence, and re-opening fences after each split.

nodes.name: transcript_parser.py
nodes.summary: JSONL transcript parser for Claude Code session files that extracts structured, display-ready messages (text, thinking, tool_use, tool_result, local_command), pairing tool_use blocks with their tool_result via tool_use_id and formatting per-tool result statistics with expandable quotes; shared by both history and real-time monitoring.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses control-character sentinels (\x02EXPQUOTE_START\x02) to mark expandable quote spans that are later rendered by the MarkdownV2 layer.

nodes.name: ParsedEntry
nodes.summary: Dataclass representing a single display-ready parsed message entry carrying role, pre-formatted text, content type, tool_use_id, timestamp, tool name, and optional decoded image data for tool results.

nodes.name: TranscriptParser
nodes.summary: Static-method parser for Claude Code JSONL session files: parses raw lines, extracts text and images, formats tool_use summaries and per-tool result statistics, and converts entry streams into flat ParsedEntry lists with tool_use/tool_result pairing and optional pending-tool carry-over for polling consumers.

nodes.name: agentic-analyze.yml

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what CCBot is: a Telegram bot that bridges each Forum topic to a tmux window running Claude Code, controlling the session by reading terminal output and sending keystrokes rather than using the Claude Code SDK. It outlines the feature set (topic-based sessions, real-time notifications, interactive UIs, voice, screenshots, message history) and the src/ccbot file structure that the rest of this tour walks through.

tour.title: Entry Point & Bootstrap
tour.description: pyproject.toml registers the `ccbot` console script whose target is main(). main.py validates the environment through config, makes sure the tmux session exists via tmux_manager, and then hands off to bot.create_bot(). bot.py is the application factory: it builds the python-telegram-bot Application, wires every command/callback/message handler, sets the bot command menu, and starts the session monitor and status-polling background tasks in post_init, tearing them down in post_shutdown.
tour.languageLesson: pyproject.toml [project.scripts] entries map a console command name to a Python callable ('ccbot = ccbot.main:main'); pip installs a thin executable that imports the module and calls main(), making entry points robust across platforms.

tour.title: Configuration & Environment
tour.description: config.py exposes a module-level `config` singleton loaded from layered .env files — the second-most imported file in the codebase, depended on by nearly every module. It requires TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and ALLOWED_USERS, defaults TMUX_SESSION_NAME, CLAUDE_COMMAND and MONITOR_POLL_INTERVAL, and scrubs sensitive env vars from spawned child processes. .env.example documents these variables so a first-time deployer knows exactly what to set.

tour.title: tmux Bridge & Session Core
tour.description: tmux_manager.py is an async-friendly wrapper around libtmux for a single tmux session — listing and finding windows, capturing panes, sending keys, renaming, creating and killing windows. SessionManager (the single most-referenced class in the graph, with a fan-in of 27) orchestrates everything around it: window↔session mappings, thread bindings, per-user read offsets, session_map.json sync, keystroke delivery and message history. Together they implement the README's core insight: control Claude Code by manipulating tmux itself.
tour.languageLesson: A module-level singleton (config and SessionManager both use it) gives every handler access to shared state without dependency injection; blocking libtmux calls are wrapped with asyncio.to_thread/executor so the PTB event loop never blocks.

tour.title: Hook-Based Session Tracking
tour.description: Because CCBot operates on tmux rather than the SDK, it learns about new sessions from a Claude Code SessionStart hook: hook.py maintains the window↔session mapping in session_map.json under a file lock and can auto-install itself into ~/.claude/settings.json. session_map_repository.py owns that file's async reads, atomic writes and flock read-modify-write discipline (shared with the hook itself), while session_migration.py converts legacy window_name keys to canonical @window_id keys at startup.
tour.languageLesson: flock file locking makes concurrent readers/writers (the hook runs inside tmux panes; the bot in a separate process) coordinate without lost updates; atomic write via temp file + rename is the standard crash-safe persistence pattern.

tour.title: Telegram Handlers & Callback Routing
tour.description: This layer turns Telegram topics into session operations. message_handlers.py routes text/photos/voice to bound tmux windows, forwards images, transcribes voice, and shells out for `!` bash commands; command_handlers.py implements /start, /history, /screenshot, /unbind and slash-command forwarding into Claude Code. Every inline button comes back through callback_router.py, which authenticates the user and dispatches CB_* payloads via exact-match and prefix registries to the callback_* sub-handlers.
tour.languageLesson: Telegram callback_data is limited to 64 bytes, so callback_data.py defines a custom prefix codec ('cb:...' typed dataclass payloads) packed into that budget — a common pattern when inline keyboards must carry rich state.

tour.title: Interactive UI & Session Creation
tour.description: interactive_ui.py detects Claude Code's interactive terminal UIs (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, Permission Prompt, RestoreCheckpoint) from captured pane text and renders them as Telegram keyboards with navigation, tracking interactive mode per user/thread — this is what makes the bot feel like a remote control rather than a dumb pipe. directory_browser.py builds the creation UX: a picker of unbound tmux windows, a paginated filesystem browser, and a session-resumption picker.

tour.title: Monitoring & Message Pipeline
tour.description: session_monitor.py (the bot's fan-out champion, message_queue.py) polls Claude Code JSONL transcripts with byte-offset tracking so it only reads new lines, emitting NewMessage events; status_polling.py runs a 1s loop checking each bound window for status lines and interactive UIs. notifications.py routes those events to the right Telegram topic via thread bindings, and message_queue.py — the highest fan-out file in the project — serializes delivery through per-user FIFO workers with flood control, content-message merging and topic-aware MessageTask.thread_id.
tour.languageLesson: asyncio background tasks (started in post_init) run concurrent services, while per-user FIFO queues guarantee Telegram messages arrive in order and respect flood limits without ever blocking the event loop.

tour.title: Parsing Output & Formatting
tour.description: Two parsers interpret what Claude Code emits: transcript_parser.py turns JSONL session entries into display-ready messages (text, thinking, tool_use paired with tool_result) and terminal_parser.py regexes captured pane text for status lines, spinners and interactive UI markers. markdown_v2.py then converts markdown via chatgpt-md-converter-equivalent telegramify wrapping, rendering tables as card-style key-value output, and telegram_sender.py chunks the text into Telegram-safe pieces measured in UTF-16 code units, re-opening fenced code blocks so every chunk stays valid.
tour.languageLesson: Telegram counts message length in UTF-16 code units (max ~4096), not characters; splitting on line boundaries while re-opening/closing code fences keeps each chunk both within limits and valid MarkdownV2.

tour.title: Persistent State
tour.description: A cluster of thin dataclass stores keeps the bot's memory across restarts: binding_store.py (thread→window bindings and group chat IDs), window_state_store.py (window_id → session/cwd/name), and monitor_state.py (per-session JSONL byte offsets so readers resume without re-sending old messages). They serialize byte-for-byte to state.json / monitor_state.json, with persistence delegated to the SessionManager facade — separating 'in-memory shape' from 'I/O strategy' makes each store trivially testable.

tour.title: Screenshots & Voice
tour.description: screenshot.py renders terminal text — including full ANSI 16/256/RGB color parsing — into dark-background PNGs via a three-tier font fallback chain, offloading the CPU-heavy rendering to a thread pool; capture_registry.py tracks active captures. transcribe.py converts Telegram voice messages to text with a lazily-initialized httpx client and no OpenAI SDK dependency. These two channels make the bot useful on mobile, where plain text from tmux would otherwise be unreadable.
tour.languageLesson: Lazy initialization (build the httpx client only on first voice message) avoids failing startup when optional capabilities are unused, while delegating CPU-bound pixel work to a thread pool keeps the async event loop responsive.

tour.title: Agentic Repair-Robot Toolkit
tour.description: A self-contained secondary subsystem under scripts/agentic: paths.py is the shared I/O API (repo-root discovery, .agentic JSON reads/writes), service.py is the single source of truth for task listing, analysis, context packs, prompts, status and validation, exported both as a CLI (cli.py wiring analyze/plan/select/propose commands) and as a stdio JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP server (mcp_server.py, tool 'ccbot-agentic'). It lets Claude Code itself drive an ANALYZE→PLAN→IMPLEMENT→VALIDATE pipeline against an issue backlog.
tour.languageLesson: MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers speak JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio: the LLM host spawns the server process and exchanges request/response frames, turning internal tooling into model-callable tools without any network service.

tour.title: Testing, CI & Putting It All Together
tour.description: The pytest suite mirrors src/ccbot 1:1 — conftest.py provides shared fixtures (JSONL row factories, sample pane renders, chrome handlers) used by tests like test_session.py that verify bindings, window state and migration. .github/workflows/check.yml runs these quality gates (ruff, pyright, pytest) across a Python 3.12/3.13 matrix on every push, and doc/telegram-bot-features.md ties the whole picture back to the Telegram API capabilities the bot exploits. Tracing the full path — entry point → bootstrap → tmux bridge → hook mapping → handlers → monitor pipeline → formatting → persistence → media → the agentic toolkit — gives the complete mental model of the project.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions uses `on` triggers to fire workflows, `jobs` for steps with `strategy.matrix` to run a job across multiple Python versions, and caching (here uv's) to speed up dependency installation; pytest-asyncio marks async tests so coroutines run inside the asyncio loop.
